definitions.statement: The Venus flytrap has no brain or nervous system, although its tissues can generate electrical and calcium signals.
definitions.caveat: Electrical excitability is not an animal nervous system; no claim about plant subjective experience.

definitions.statement: In this story, short-term memory means that a temporary biochemical state retains information about recent stimulation and can affect a later response; it is not conscious recollection.
definitions.caveat: Functional interpretation of observed signal persistence and timing; not proof of consciousness or the absence of all other information-storage mechanisms.

definitions.statement: A sufficiently effective sensory-hair deflection can generate an action potential that propagates through the trap.
definitions.caveat: A contact is not always anAP; amplitude and movement speed matter. No axons or neuronal network implied.

definitions.statement: In the tested brief-deflection regime, one action potential can occur while the trap remains open; a single AP was insufficient to cause the rapid closing response.
definitions.caveat: Conditional tested regime, not every first physical touch or every possible activation method.

definitions.statement: In transgenic calcium-reporter experiments, sensory-hair stimulation raised cytosolic calcium-associated fluorescence, starting near the hair and spreading into leaf tissue.
definitions.caveat: Fluorescent proxy and measured tissue regions; no literal calcium light or precise localization to all cells.

definitions.statement: Electrical excitation and cytosolic calcium changes are coupled components of the trap response; the narration distinguishes them and describes the calcium rise as accompanying the signal.
definitions.caveat: Does not settle exact causal order or propagation speeds.2020paper noted setup-dependent distinctions;2023review discusses co-propagation.

definitions.statement: After the first stimulus, the calcium-reporter response rose and then gradually declined in the measured leaf regions.
definitions.caveat: The2020paper fit two-phase exponential decay; qualitative tint is not a linear or exact fit.

definitions.statement: The residual calcium-reporter signal before a second stimulus was significantly associated with whether the leaf closed in the2020experiments.
definitions.caveat: Residual state correlates with response, not an independently isolated sole memory molecule. Fig3d/e decay observations used6leaves from2plants.

definitions.statement: A second sufficiently nearby stimulus raised the calcium-reporter response above the first response in the tested leaf regions, consistent with accumulation of recent signals.
definitions.caveat: The addition is a biological response, not arithmetic of identical calcium packets or moving fluid.

definitions.statement: The2020study supports a putative calcium-response threshold associated with trap closure; a sufficiently elevated response can accompany snapping shut.
definitions.caveat: Thresholds inferred from relative reporter intensity and closure probabilities. Region dependence, reporter saturation and rapid movement limit measurement. No universal scalar cutoff, sole-cause claim or guarantee from calcium level alone.

definitions.statement: As the earlier calcium response decays, a later stimulus may fail to elevate the response enough for closure; timing therefore changes the outcome.
definitions.caveat: Conditional response, not a hard30-second boundary; full causal bridge to mechanical motion remains outside this explanation.

definitions.statement: One suitably slower sensory-hair deflection can generate two action potentials, either during bending or during bending and return, and trigger trap closure.
definitions.caveat: Intermediate tested angular velocity, not all slow movements. Holding the hair motionless is distinct and was not sufficient in tested static-displacement trials.

definitions.statement: The study visualized calcium dynamics using transgenicGCaMP6f and fluorescence microscopy; the depicted calcium tint in the proposed film is an explanatory visualization.
definitions.caveat: No naturally glowing plant or raw-measurement authenticity implied. Methods also describe pseudocoloring.

definitions.statement: A typical trap has six inner sensory hairs, three on each lobe; these are distinct from the marginal cilia.
definitions.caveat: Geometry must not confuse marginal teeth with trigger hairs; do not invent exact cell arrangement.

definitions.statement: Suda et al. reported a fitted50-percent-closure duration of30.88seconds, with95-percentconfidence interval21.4–45.42seconds, in a30-observation logistic analysis.
definitions.caveat: A fitted association with reported experimental conditioning, not every plant’s memory lifetime. Unselected numerical detail; Table1text/caption inspected, screenshot unavailable.

definitions.statement: The2023New Phytologist review summarizes the first-AP memory as approximately20seconds.
definitions.caveat: Review summary differs from2020fitted~30secondrelationship. Do not manufacture a measured20–30secondrange or average.

definitions.statement: A2026primary study reports epidermal cell-wall softening rather than water transport as the rapid mechanical driver releasing stored elastic energy.
definitions.caveat: Original abstract inspected, fulltext inaccessible. Scientific result attributed to that study, not independently reanalyzed; not selected for the memory narration.

definitions.statement: The2020study localized all relevant calcium memory to one identifiable cell type.
definitions.caveat: Unresolved/excluded from visuals: authors could not localize fluorescence to specific deep intact cells. No named memorycell.

definitions.statement: Exactly two separate physical touches are universally required to close a Venus flytrap.
definitions.caveat: False shortcut; movement/APmapping depends on amplitude/speed and a singledeflectioncan2APs.

definitions.statement: Every flytrap completely erases its memory at exactly30seconds.
definitions.caveat: Unsupported universal/digital reset; source statistics and differing summaries exclude it.

definitions.statement: Every physical touch produces exactly one electrical signal.
definitions.caveat: False: noAP,oneAPor2APs can occur under different movement conditions.

definitions.statement: Calcium signaling naturally produces naked-eye glowing light in ordinary flytrap leaves.
definitions.caveat: Engineered reporter and imaging light, not intrinsic bioluminescence.

definitions.statement: The reported signal integration proves that Venus flytraps consciously remember and perform arithmetic.
definitions.caveat: Data establish biochemical responses, not conscious recollection or numerical concepts.

definitions.statement: Keeping a hair bent motionlessly for30seconds necessarily produces twoAPs and closure.
definitions.caveat: Tested static-displacementtrials n11 did not close; slowmovingdeflectionis different.

definitions.statement: Rapid water transport is the settled demonstrated motor mechanism behind the snap in this story.
definitions.caveat: Older explanatory model is challenged by2026primaryabstract; do not animate rapid pumping as established.

definitions.statement: A single absolute calcium concentration universally guarantees closure in all flytrap cells and specimens.
definitions.caveat: No sufficient calibration, universal celllocalization or probability-one threshold in inspected evidence.

definitions.statement: The full molecular pathway from calcium/electrical signaling to mechanical wall softening is completely resolved by the inspected studies.
definitions.caveat: Memoryintegration explanation does not claim a full mechanical causal chain; no direct bridge verified here.
